name: veterinary_clinic_system_074_cross_location_patient_moves
instruction: Audit the inter-location patient transfer ledger for the operations review, batched under the episode batch code in ops_reports. The transfer log is not enough by itself — a transfer may be marked completed while the patient is actually somewhere else, and the audit_log may not contain a completion record for every completed move. Create one ops_reports row with report='transfer_matrix': {batch_code, matrix, pending_total, completed_total, approved_total, most_active_lane}. matrix is a JSON object mapping 'from->to' to the count of location_transfers rows with that pair across all statuses. pending_total, completed_total, and approved_total are the counts by status. most_active_lane is the 'from->to' key with the most transfers; tie -> alphabetically first. Then create one ops_reports row with report='transfer_reconciliation': {batch_code, stale_completed_count, completed_without_audit_count, pending_source_mismatch_count, duplicate_patient_count}. stale_completed_count = number of completed transfers where the patient's current location_id does not equal the transfer's to_location_id. completed_without_audit_count = number of completed transfers whose patient_id is not the target_id of any audit_log row with action='TRANSFER_COMPLETED' and target_collection='patients'. pending_source_mismatch_count = number of pending transfers where the patient's current location_id does not equal the transfer's from_location_id. duplicate_patient_count = number of patients with more than one transfer row. Then create one ops_reports row per pending transfer (sorted by transfer_id) with report='transfer_review': {batch_code, transfer_id, patient_id, patient_name, owner_id, owner_name, from_location_id, from_location_name, to_location_id, to_location_name, note, ready}. ready = true iff the patient is still at the source location and has no appointment already scheduled at the destination location. No collection outside ops_reports may be modified.
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session

success_criteria.summary: Recompute the transfer matrix, status totals, most-active lane (with tiebreak), and the reconciliation counts from live location_transfers, patients, audit_log, and appointments. One transfer_review row per pending transfer with the ready flag derived from the patient's current location and any destination appointment. Every aggregate verified by both a raw-row Python pass and an independent SQL pass.

checks.expect: matrix/status totals/reconciliation counts computed by raw-row filter and SQL agree with each other and the written rows

hazards: The transfer matrix counts all statuses; lanes '1->2' and '1->3' are tied at 2 transfers each, so the deterministic tiebreak matters — most_active_lane must be '1->2'.

Completed transfers can be stale: transfer id=5 (patient 26, from 2 to 1, status 'completed') does not match the patient's current location (patient 26 is at location 3 because a later completed transfer id=6 moved it to 3). An agent that only checks the latest completed transfer per patient will miss this.

Two of the three completed transfers (id=5 and id=6, both patient 26) have no audit_log row with action='TRANSFER_COMPLETED' and target_collection='patients'; only transfer id=3 (patient 15) has one. An agent that does not join to audit_log will report completed_without_audit_count=0.

Pending transfer id=7 (patient 30, from 1 to 2, status 'pending') is a decoy: patient 30's current location is already 3, not 1, so pending_source_mismatch_count is 1 and the review row's ready flag must be false. An agent that trusts the transfer row without checking the patient registry gets this wrong.

Approved transfer id=4 (patient 19, from 3 to 2, status 'approved') already has the patient at the destination; it should be counted in approved_total but not in pending_source_mismatch_count or stale_completed_count.
Patient 26 has two transfer rows (id=5 and id=6); duplicate_patient_count is 1, not 2 — it counts patients with more than one row, not the extra rows themselves.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Fuses a transfer-lane matrix with a reconciliation against the patient registry, the audit log, and the appointment schedule; includes a stale-completed decoy, a pending-source-mismatch decoy, and a deterministic most-active-lane tiebreak.
